caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 892 of 2017.
lawyer:
AJ Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate (with Joined Abedin, Senior Advocate) with Raghib Rauf Chowdhury; Advocate, instructed by Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record------For the Petitioner 
Mahbubey Alam, Attorney-General with Khurshid Alanz Khan, Advocate instructed by Sufia Khanna, Advocate-on-Record-----------For Respondent No. 2. 
None Represented----------Respondent No. 1.
parties:
Begum Khaleda Zia -------- Petitioner

State & another --------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J : The petitioner has filed this leave petition against the judgment and order dated 20-8-2017 pissed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 36282 of 2017 rejecting the application under section 10(3); of the Criminal Amendment Act, 1958. 

 2. Short facts, for the disposal of this petition, are that the petitioner is an accused of Special Case No.- 17 of 2017 corresponding to ACC GR No. 102 of 2008 arising out of Ramna PS Case No. 8 dated 3-7-2008 under section 5(2) of Act 11 1947 read with sections 409/109 of the Penal Code, at present, pending in the 5th Court of Special Judge, Dhaka. She filed instant application in the High Court Division for transfer of the aforesaid case on the grounds amongst others that it has been witnessed on 24-4-2017 by all the learned counsel for the petitioner and persons present in the Court that the Special Judge had verbally ordered to arrest one of the learned counsel, namely, Mr AM Mahbubuddin Khokon, Secretary of the Supreme Court Bar Association, which was subsequently recalled, while he was trying to submit the case of the petitioner, supplementing the submissions of other learned counsel. Such an incident demonstrates that the Special Judge is biased towards the prosecution and is intending to obstruct the learned counsel for the petitioner from presenting the case of the petitioner. The Special Judge created a frightening situation on 3-8-2017 upon calling RAB and police while the senior lawyers like Mr Jamiruddin Sircar, Mr Khondaker Mahbub Hossain, Mr AJ Mohammad Ali and Mr Abdur Razzaq Khan were trying to satisfy the court for getting adjournment of the case considering the illness of the accused petitioner who had been taking treatment abroad. Such behaviour of the learned Judge does not fall within the norms of judicial functions and the petitioner apprehends that she would not get justice, from that court. That the presiding Judge of the Special Court did not provide certified copy of the orders dated 27-7-2017 and 3-8-2017 in spite of repeated attempts to obtain the same by the learned lawyers of the petitioner and such conduct of the learned Judge demonstrates his convicting mind and be the case as it may the petitioner apprehends that she would not get justice from that court. That the orders of the learned Judge pertaining to refusing several applications for adjournments and/or for recalling the witness for cross-examination demonstrate that those are like a full pledged judgment upon framing issues and giving findings on it and such orders ex-facie demonstrates that the learned Judge has always tried to bring the learned counsel for the petitioner on the dock accusing them for delaying the process even if the legal questions are raised. That in respect of other cases of similar nature, the Special Judge usually grant adjournment for one month or more but in the case of the instant petitioner the date is fixed between 377 days which demonstrates his special interest. 

 3. The High Court Division, by the .impugned judgment and order, rejected the said application holding that the case was initiated on 5-8-2009; Charge was framed on 19-3-2014; Prosecution examined 32 witnesses and that 26 adjournments were given, for examination of the accused petitioner under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and still the case is awaiting for the same and that the superior court directed the Special Judge to conclude the trial within certain time and that the petitioner went abroad without informing the court. The High Court Division also did not find any merit to the allegation of not getting fair justice from the Presiding Judge of the Court. 

 4. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner, submits that the petitioner apprehends that she would not get fair and impartial justice from the presiding judge of the Special Court No. 5, Dhaka. He submits that since the presiding judge had been fixing the case for hearing in every week and once he orally directed the police to arrest Mr AM Mahbubuddin Khokon, learned Counsel for the petitioner and Secretary of the Supreme Court Bar Association and that the environment of the court room is not favourable for the accused, learned counsel and audience present in the Court, the case is required to be transferred in any other Court of competent jurisdiction. He further submits that the petitioner genuinely apprehends that the presiding Judge is biased in conducting the case since he rejected the petitioner's applications for recalling the witnesses and adjournments. 

 5. Mr Khurshid Alam Kham, learned Counsel appearing for the Anti Corruption Commission, submits that the petitioner, in fact, went to the High Court Division against each and every order except the orders relating to the prayers for adjournment. He submits that the petitioner took adjournments 33 times for her examination under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the lawyers of the accused petitioners and the petitioner herself obstructed the court proceeding in every possible step so that the presiding Judge of the Court could not proceed with the case smoothly in accordance with law. He submits that the presiding Judge is well behaved and he is very cautious about the social position of the petitioner and in every step he urged the learned lawyers of the accused persons as well as others present in the Court room to co-operate with the court for proper, smooth and effective adjudication of the case in accordance with law. He submits that the petitioner has filed the application for transfer of the case at the fag end of the same only to delay its disposal. 

 6. It appears from the order of the High Court Division that on that particular date the learned Public Prosecutor filed application for cancellation of bail of the petitioner consequently, situation was into being and lastly, that unwanted situation was resolved at the instance of the learned leading Senior Lawyers of the Supreme Court Bar. That is, first ground for transfer of the case, that the court verbally ordered arrest of Mr AM Mahbubuddin Khokon, which was recalled instantly at the interference of the learned Senior Counsel present in the Court room, does not carry any force in view of the fact that the presiding Judge and learned Counsel present Mutually resolved the situation and, accordingly, the Court honoured the approach of the learned Counsel. The Bench and Bar being two integral parts of the administration of justice, both must conduct themselves in such a way that that prestige and image are maintained and the case may be adjudicated smoothly and effectively in accordance with law. In the case of Md Nurul Alam vs Sohail Thakur reported in 20 BLD (AD) 85 = 5 BLC (AD) 111, this Division has observed. 

 "It must be said that the High Court Division was entirely wrong in reading a basis for apprehension in the mind of the accused about fair trial from the mere fact that during trial their bails was cancelled by the courts concerned only to ensure a speedy conclusion of the trial. It has 'been noticed that the bail was cancelled exactly for the said purpose as the trial was being dragged on for certain lapses on the part of the accused who were on bail on different dates. It is not unusual that the accused persons who remain on bail are taken into custody during trial for holding a quick trial without unforeseen interruptions. The taking of custody of the accused in the midst of the trial was therefore neither unusual nor such a thing as would suggest bias or preconceiveness in the mind of the court against the accused. The High Court Division ought to have been aware of this ordinary procedure adopted in the trial of Sessions cases. If such ground as was considered sufficient for apprehension in the mind of the accused in the present case is to be upheld then the High Court Division will be flooded with transfer applications." 

 7. The second ground for getting the case transferred was that an environment of the Court room is not favourable for the accused, learned Counsel and the audience. It is becoming a frequent phenomenon in our country that court proceedings are being disturbed by hoodlums and unruly disrupting the judicial hearing with menaces, noises and worse. It is the obligation of all concerned to maintain congenial atmosphere in the Court room which is the wish of the Judge presiding the Court as well. It is pious expectation from the presiding Judge, learned Counsel of both the parties, audience present in the Court room and law enforcing agencies that all of them should help each other for maintaining congenial environment in the court room. Every one shall co-operate the Court in that regard. Mere allegation like substantial prejudice, non-availability of the congenial atmosphere for a free trial cannot be the ground for transfer of a case. 

 8. One of the grounds for which the petitioner sought transfer of the case is that on 8-8-2017 the Special Judge created a frightening situation upon calling RAB and police while the Senior Lawyers were trying to satisfy the court to grant adjournment. It is difficult to accept such ground as reasonable one that the presiding judge is biased so he deployed law enforcing agency in the premises. 

 9. It is relevant here to quote a passage from the case of Gurcharan Dass Chadha vs Rajesthan reported in AIR 1966 SC 1418 where it was observed by the Supreme Court of India that a mere allegation that there is apprehension that justice will not be done in a given case does not suffice. The Court has further to see whether the apprehension is reasonable or not. To judge of the reasonableness of the apprehension the state of the mind of the person who entertains the apprehension is no doubt relevant but that is not all. The apprehension must not only be entertained, but must appear to the Court to be a reasonable apprehension. 

 10. In the case of Abdul Nazar Madani vs State of Tanzil Nadu reported in AIR 2000 SC 2293 it was observed that the mere existence of a surcharged atmosphere without there being proof of inability for holding fair and impartial trial cannot be made a ground for transfer of a case. 

 12. Taking into consideration the entire facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, we are of the view that the petitioner has failed to make out a case that she has reasonable apprehension of not availing justice from the presiding Judge of the Special Court No. 5, Dhaka. 

 13. A transfer should not readily be granted for any imaginative ground of a litigant. Where the ground for transfer is not substantiated as such does not exist, case cannot be transferred.
